title: Digital Reading with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): A proof-of-concept study on the cognitive effects of visual display options
summary: Reading longer or more difficult texts can be a challenge for people with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This study takes this as an opportunity to examine differences in reading behavior between adults with ADHD and healthy control participants. The aim of the study is to determine whether different visual presentation options can support people with ADHD in digital reading. Five display options are considered: (1) highlighting the line currently being read, (2) highlighting the word currently in focus, (3) blurring the lines not in focus, (4) Bionic Reading, in which the first letters of the words are highlighted, and (5) no highlighting. In addition to the primary objective, the study aims to compare different visual text display options to determine whether certain variants might be more helpful for people with ADHD than others, and whether people with ADHD and healthy control participants differ in their reading behaviour and reactions to the various visual display options. During the study, participants are asked to read texts presented in the specified display options. Various measurement sensors (including eye-tracking and electroencephalography) and questionnaires are used to record reading behaviour and attention levels. In addition, participants are asked about their mental effort, perceived benefits and reading comprehension.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Normal or corrected vision
- Sufficient knowledge of German at a minimum of CEFR level B2
- Healthy control group: neurologically and psychologically inconspicuous adults without any diagnosed psychiatric and neurological disorders
- ADHD group: An ADHD diagnosis must be supported by a suitable document. Acceptable documents include, for example, a medical or psychological diagnostic report, a clinical report, a medical certificate, a doctor’s letter, or a medication plan or prescription for an ADHD-specific medication. If no such document is available, the study coordinator is to be contacted; mild to moderate mental health comorbidities, in particular mood disorders and anxiety disorders, are permitted
Exclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed dyslexia or dyscalculia, 
- Severe psychiatric disorders (e.g. schizophrenia or severe affective disorders), 
- Acute mental health crises, 
- Neurological conditions (including visual impairments such as visual field defects or achromatopsia (colour blindness))
- Current alcohol or drug addiction
- Insufficient German language proficiency (below CEFR level B2).
- If two pairs of glasses must be worn one on top of the other, this will result in exclusion
